decisions.reason: Because A is a differentiated but still core cardboard display and has already survived the early uncertainty period, management would likely see no clear performance shortfall versus aspirations and retain it.

C remains close to the established quarter-pallet display business, so absent evidence of results below internal or peer aspiration levels the firm would usually keep it, though its overlap with the core range gives some pruning risk.

F fits existing capabilities but serves a narrower media niche, so management would probably continue it while monitoring performance, with a somewhat higher withdrawal risk if that niche underperforms relative to aspirations.
